dialogue:
A: So, you know, I was thinking about Taiwan's performance in the World Baseball Classic this year. It’s kind of a bummer how they got eliminated, right? 

B: Oh, totally! I mean, they had some highs and lows, but that tiebreaker situation was just brutal. Can you imagine being tied with two other teams and still not making it through?

A: Right? And that loss to Japan, like 13-0, must’ve felt like a punch to the gut. You gotta wonder how much that affected their confidence moving forward.

B: For sure! And then they bounced back with that 14-0 win against the Czech Republic, which must’ve been a huge morale boost. It’s like, “We can do this!” But then that nail-biter against South Korea in 10 innings? Heart-stopping!

A: Exactly! And the fact that they only advanced to the quarterfinals once in the past six WBCs just shows how tough it is. I mean, you’d think they’d be able to build on their home soil advantage from last time.

B: Yeah, I was really hoping they’d get further this year, especially with Hao-Jin Tseng taking over as manager. I mean, he was a hitting coach before, so it’s like a whole new game plan, right?

A: Oh, for sure! And he mentioned he’d be showing a “poker face” this time around. Like, what does that even mean? Is he trying to be intimidating or just really focused?

B: Haha, probably a bit of both! But I think a serious approach could help them, especially in crucial games. It’s like when you’re playing poker—sometimes, you just gotta keep a straight face to keep the other team guessing.

A: Exactly! And you know, with the talent they’ve got, I really hope they can pull together next time. They’ve shown flashes of brilliance, and it’s just a matter of putting it all together, right?

B: Totally! I mean, who knows? Maybe next WBC, they’ll finally break that quarterfinal curse and surprise everyone. I’d love to see that!

SOURCE TITLE: Taiwan eliminated from WBC following South Korea's 7-2 win over ...
SOURCE CONTENT: WBC / Taiwan eliminated from WBC following South Korea's 7-2 win over Australia
Taipei, March 9 (CNA) Team Taiwan's 2026 World Baseball Classic (WBC) journey ended Monday night when South Korea beat Australia 7-2 and won the tiebreaker with Australia and Taiwan to advance to the tournament's quarterfinals in Miami.
South Korea earned its spot by scoring a run in the top of the ninth to do just enough under the tiebreaker rules to advance.
The result saw Taiwan, South Korea, and Australia tied for second in WBC Pool C behind undefeated Japan with 2-2 records.
The tiebreaker was determined by dividing a team's total runs allowed by the total number of defensive outs in games among the tied teams, and with the three teams all allowing seven runs in their games, it came down to the smallest margin.
The Koreans got the nod because they recorded a total of 57 outs in their games against the tied teams (including a 10-inning 5-4 loss to Taiwan) while Taiwan and Australia recorded the regulation 54 outs.
Taiwan will rue its ugly start to the WBC, when it could muster only three hits in a 3-0 loss to Australia. Because Australia was the home team, Taiwan only recorded 24 outs, putting it at a disadvantage in determining who finished second.
A run scored or one fewer run allowed by Taiwan may have meant the difference in the final tiebreaker.
After an awful 13-0 loss in seven innings due to the mercy rule to Japan, Taiwan whipped the Czech Republic 14-0 in seven innings before outlasting South Korea 5-4 in 10 innings, giving it a sliver of hope of advancing.
In six WBCs played, Taiwan has only advanced to the quarterfinals once, in 2013.
Japan will complete Pool C play on Tuesday night against the Czech Republic, having already clinched the top spot in the group.

SOURCE TITLE: Team Chinese Taipei 2026 World Baseball Classic preview
SOURCE CONTENT: The last time Hao-Jin Tseng was in the World Baseball Classic, he was serving as the hitting coach for Team Chinese Taipei in 2023. Three years later, he’ll be back on that same international stage, this time as the club’s manager. With this transition to a bigger role, opponents may notice a different approach from him than the one they saw at the last WBC.
“Not as much smiling,” Tseng said via translator Chien-Ting Lin at MLB’s Winter Meetings in December. “With more responsibilities, I always show them a poker face.”
The new approach seemed to work wonders back in November of 2024, when, under Tseng's watch, Team Chinese Taipei won its first gold medal at the senior level during the Premier12 tournament. And though Tseng will be doing his best to mask his feelings again come this March, his club is undoubtedly eager to ride that momentum and return to the Classic after its thrilling 2023 run on home soil came to a heartbreaking end. With high expectations and a slew of formidable group play foes, Team Chinese Taipei heads to Tokyo this March vying to advance beyond its pool for the first time since 2013.
2023 WBC Performance
Team Chinese Taipei endured a roller-coaster 2023 World Baseball Classic experience while playing in front of home fans whose trademark stadium atmosphere caught the baseball world by storm. After dropping its opening Pool A game against Panama, Chinese Taipei rallied late to topple Italy before beating the Netherlands the next day, thanks in part to a supernova performance from infielder and former big leaguer Yu Chang.
